scenario: 面试白板/共享编辑器上写 OOD 的类和 API。
scenario_en: Writing OOD classes and APIs on the whiteboard / shared editor in an interview.
q: 为什么要在意命名和大小写的约定？
q_en: Why care about naming and casing conventions?
options: 一致、地道的命名一眼传达工程成熟度，也降低阅读认知负担
约定纯属个人审美，选哪种、混着用都完全没有影响，面试官根本不看这些细节
只有编译器强制的规则才重要，其余风格随意
命名越花哨越显得有创意
options_en: Consistent, idiomatic naming signals maturity at a glance and lowers reading load
Conventions are pure personal taste; mixing them has zero impact and interviewers never look at such details
Only compiler-enforced rules matter; everything else is free-form
The fancier the names, the more creative you look
optionExplanations: 对：地道命名是低成本的高信号——第一眼就传达「这人写过生产代码」，还让读者省力。
错：面试官恰恰会从命名一致性判断工程成熟度。
错：可读性约定虽不被编译器强制，却直接影响评价。
错：花哨≠专业，清晰表意才是。
optionExplanations_en: Right: idiomatic naming is a low-cost, high-signal cue — it says "this person has shipped code" and eases reading.
Wrong: interviewers do judge engineering maturity from naming consistency.
Wrong: readability conventions are not compiler-enforced but directly shape evaluation.
Wrong: fancy is not professional; clear intent is.
why: 命名约定低成本高信号:一致、地道的命名让面试官一眼觉得你写过生产代码,也降低阅读负担。它不被编译器强制,却实打实影响「工程成熟度」评价——别混用,跟语言惯例走。
why_en: Naming conventions are low-cost, high-signal: consistent, idiomatic names make an interviewer feel you have shipped real code and lower reading load. They are not compiler-enforced yet materially shape the "engineering maturity" impression — so do not mix styles; follow the language's idiom.
tradeoff: 一致地道的命名(读起来省力·显工程成熟度) vs 各写各的风格(当场少想一步·换来阅读与评价成本)

scenario: 先认全常见的几种大小写风格。
scenario_en: First, recognize the common casing styles.
options_en: camelCase (lower camel)
PascalCase (upper camel)
snake_case
kebab-case
optionExplanations: 对：首字母小写、后续单词首字母大写 = camelCase。
错：PascalCase 是首字母也大写(GetUserProfile)。
错：snake_case 是全小写加下划线(get_user_profile)。
错：kebab-case 是全小写加连字符(get-user-profile)。
optionExplanations_en: Right: first letter lower, subsequent words capitalized = camelCase.
Wrong: PascalCase also capitalizes the first letter (GetUserProfile).
Wrong: snake_case is all-lower with underscores (get_user_profile).
Wrong: kebab-case is all-lower with hyphens (get-user-profile).
why: 五种大小写:camelCase、PascalCase、snake_case、SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE、kebab-case,分别用于 方法/类/Python方法/常量/URL。认清它们是后面所有约定的基础。
why_en: Five styles: camelCase (getUser), PascalCase (GetUser/ClassName), snake_case (get_user), SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (MAX_SIZE), kebab-case (get-user). Recognizing them underpins every convention that follows.

rows: 几乎所有语言的类/类型名

scenario: 给停车场 OOD 里的类命名。
scenario_en: Naming classes in a parking-lot OOD.
q: 类 / 类型名该用哪种大小写？
q_en: What casing do class/type names use?
options_en: PascalCase: ParkingLot, PaymentMethod
camelCase: parkingLot, paymentMethod
snake_case: parking_lot, payment_method
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE: PARKING_LOT
optionExplanations: 对：从 Java 到 Go、Swift、Python,类与枚举类型一律首字母大写驼峰,几乎无例外。
错：camelCase 是给方法/变量的,不是类。
错：snake_case 类名在主流语言里都不地道。
错：全大写是常量,不是类。
optionExplanations_en: Right: from Java to Go, Swift and Python, classes and enum types all take upper-camel, with almost no exceptions.
Wrong: camelCase is for methods/variables, not classes.
Wrong: a snake_case class name is non-idiomatic in every mainstream language.
Wrong: all-caps is for constants, not classes.
why: 类/类型/枚举类型名用 PascalCase(首字母大写驼峰):ParkingLot、PaymentMethod、VehicleType。几乎跨所有主流语言通用,是最不会错的一条,先刻进肌肉。
why_en: Class/type/enum-type names use PascalCase (upper camel): ParkingLot, PaymentMethod, VehicleType. This is near-universal across mainstream languages and the safest rule — make it muscle memory.
tradeoff: 类型名恒 PascalCase(跨语言通用) vs camelCase/snake_case(留给方法与变量)——类型层与成员层分开

scenario: 给方法和变量命名——这一步最容易露怯。
scenario_en: Naming methods and variables — where amateurism shows most.
q: 方法 / 变量该用 camelCase 还是 snake_case？
options: 看语言：Java/JS 用 camelCase，Python 用 snake_case
不分语言，所有语言的方法和变量都统一用 camelCase，这样最省事、跨语言也最一致
所有语言都统一用 snake_case
方法用 PascalCase 才显得正式
options_en: Depends on language: camelCase in Java/JS, snake_case in Python
Ignore the language; uniformly use camelCase for methods and variables everywhere — simplest and most consistent across languages
All languages uniformly use snake_case
Methods should be PascalCase to look formal
optionExplanations: 对：方法/变量大小写是语言相关的——用错(如 Java 里写 snake_case)一眼就露外行。
错：camelCase 方法名只在 Java/JS/C#/Kotlin 圈子里地道,搬进 Python 就露怯。
错：Java/JS/C# 的方法是 camelCase,不是 snake_case。
错：PascalCase 是类名;方法用它在多数语言里都不对(Go 的导出规则例外)。
optionExplanations_en: Right: method/variable casing is language-dependent — using the wrong one (e.g. snake_case in Java) instantly reads as amateur.
Wrong: camelCase method names are idiomatic only in the Java/JS/C#/Kotlin world; carried into Python they look off.
Wrong: Java/JS/C# methods are camelCase, not snake_case.
Wrong: PascalCase is for classes; using it for methods is wrong in most languages (Go's export rule aside).
why: 方法/变量大小写跟语言走:camelCase 阵营(Java/JS/C#…)vs snake_case 阵营(Python/Ruby/Rust)。类名恒 PascalCase;方法搞混(Java 写 get_user)一眼外行。
why_en: This is the biggest professionalism tell: method/variable casing follows the language — the camelCase camp (Java/JS/TS/C#/Kotlin/Swift) vs the snake_case camp (Python/Ruby/Rust). Class names are PascalCase everywhere, but do not mix methods: get_user in Java or getUser in Python instantly looks amateur.
tradeoff: camelCase 阵营(Java/JS/C#/Kotlin/Swift) vs snake_case 阵营(Python/Ruby/Rust)——方法/变量随语言,类名恒 PascalCase

scenario: 定义一个「最大重试次数」的常量。
options: PascalCase：MaxRetries（在多数语言里看起来像个类名）
options_en: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE: MAX_RETRIES
camelCase: maxRetries
PascalCase: MaxRetries (looks like a class name in most languages)
Anything; constants have no convention
optionExplanations: 对：全大写下划线在一屏代码里自成一类,读者立刻知道不该在运行时改它。
错：camelCase 是普通变量,读者分不出它是常量。
错：PascalCase 在多数语言里像类名(C# 是例外)。
错：常量有明确约定,不能随便。
optionExplanations_en: Right: all-caps-underscore stands out on screen, so readers instantly know it must not be mutated at runtime.
Wrong: camelCase reads as an ordinary variable; readers cannot tell it is constant.
Wrong: PascalCase looks like a class name in most languages (C# is the exception).
Wrong: constants do have a clear convention.
why: 常量用 SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE(全大写+下划线):MAX_RETRIES。通行于 Java/JS/Python/C++,一眼传达「不可变配置值」。(Go/C# 例外,用 PascalCase。)
why_en: Constants use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (all-caps + underscores): MAX_RETRIES, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS. Common in Java/JS/Python/C++; it signals "immutable config value" at a glance. (Go/C# are exceptions, using PascalCase.)

scenario: 给类和方法起名时的语义规则。
scenario_en: The semantic rule when naming classes and methods.
q: 类名和方法名在词性上应该是？
q_en: What part of speech should class vs method names be?
options: 类名用动词、方法名用名词
类名和方法名都统一用名词就行，不用区分词性
options_en: class = noun, method = verb phrase
Class names are verbs; method names are nouns
Both class and method names can just be nouns, no need to distinguish
Part of speech does not matter as long as it runs
optionExplanations: 对：类=事物(名词)、方法=动作(动词),读代码像读句子,意图自明。
错：反过来会让 API 读起来别扭(order.paymentProcessor() ？)。
错：方法用名词(order.payment())读者不知道它「做」什么。
错：词性直接决定可读性,不是能跑就行。
optionExplanations_en: Right: class = thing (noun), method = action (verb); code reads like sentences and intent is self-evident.
Wrong: reversing makes APIs awkward (order.paymentProcessor()?).
Wrong: a noun method (order.payment()) hides what it does.
Wrong: part of speech drives readability; "it runs" is not enough.
why: 类名用名词(是什么:Order、PaymentProcessor),方法名用动词短语(做什么:createOrder、chargeCard、isExpired)。这样 order.charge(card) 读起来就是一句话,意图自明。
why_en: Class names are nouns (what it is: Order, PaymentProcessor); method names are verb phrases (what it does: createOrder, chargeCard, isExpired). Then `order.charge(card)` reads like a sentence with self-evident intent. Query methods often start with get/is/has.
tradeoff: 类=名词、方法=动词(调用处读成一句话) vs 词性混用(order.paymentProcessor() 这类别扭 API)

scenario: 给一个表示「账号是否激活」的布尔字段/方法命名。
scenario_en: Naming a boolean field/method for "is the account active".
q: 布尔值怎么命名最专业？
q_en: How to name a boolean most professionally?
options: 用名词：active、permission、dispense，读到时再自己判断
用 flag1、flag2 这类通用名
options_en: is/has/can prefix: isActive, hasPermission
Nouns: active, permission, dispense — judge for yourself when reading
Use generic names like flag1, flag2
Use imperative verbs: activate, dispense
optionExplanations: 对：is/has/can 前缀让 `if (user.isActive)` 读起来就是个真假判断,一眼知道是布尔。
错：裸名词读者分不清是布尔还是对象。
错：flag1/flag2 毫无表意。
错：activate 像个会改状态的动作方法,不是布尔查询。
optionExplanations_en: Right: an is/has/can prefix makes `if (user.isActive)` read as a truth test — obviously boolean.
Wrong: a bare noun leaves readers unsure if it is a boolean or an object.
Wrong: flag1/flag2 conveys nothing.
Wrong: activate looks like a state-changing action, not a boolean query.
why: 布尔用 is/has/can 前缀,让它读起来像个是非判断:isActive、canDispense。if(order.isPaid) 一眼可读;裸名词 if(order.paid) 就含糊,分不清布尔还是对象。
why_en: Booleans take an is/has/can/should prefix so they read as a yes/no test: isActive, hasPermission, canDispense, isExpired. `if (order.isPaid)` reads clearly; a bare noun `if (order.paid)` is ambiguous about whether it is a boolean or an object.
tradeoff: is/has/can 前缀(读作是非判断) vs 裸名词 paid(短一点·代价是分不清布尔还是对象)

scenario: 给「校验规则」的接口/抽象基类命名。
scenario_en: Naming the interface/abstract base for a "validation rule".
q_en: How should you name an interface?
options: 统一加匈牙利前缀 I：IValidationRule、IPaymentMethod（多数语言不推荐）
在名字里带上具体实现：CreditCardValidationRuleImpl
options_en: PascalCase noun or -able: ValidationRule, Comparable
Prefix everything with Hungarian I: IValidationRule, IPaymentMethod (discouraged in most languages)
Lowercase snake_case: validation_rule
Bake the concrete impl into the name: CreditCardValidationRuleImpl
optionExplanations: 对：接口是 PascalCase 名词或能力形容词(-able);它描述「能力/角色」,不该暴露实现。
错：I 前缀是 C#/旧 COM 习惯,Java/Python/Go/Swift 里不地道。
错：接口不用 snake_case,类型名恒 PascalCase。
错：接口名不该带 Impl/具体实现,那是给实现类留的。
optionExplanations_en: Right: an interface is a PascalCase noun or capability adjective (-able); it names a capability/role and should not leak the implementation.
Wrong: the I prefix is a C#/legacy-COM habit, non-idiomatic in Java/Python/Go/Swift.
Wrong: interfaces are not snake_case; type names are always PascalCase.
Wrong: an interface name should not contain Impl/a concrete implementation — that is for the impl class.
why: 接口/抽象类用 PascalCase,取名反映能力或角色:名词(ValidationRule)或 -able(Comparable)。别用匈牙利 IFoo(除 C#),也别把具体实现塞进接口名。
why_en: Interfaces/abstract classes are PascalCase, named for a capability or role: a noun (ValidationRule, PaymentMethod) or an -able adjective (Comparable, Iterable). Avoid Hungarian IFoo (outside the C# ecosystem) and do not bake a concrete implementation into the interface name. The impl class carries specificity: CreditCardPayment implements PaymentMethod.
tradeoff: 名词/-able 接口名(表能力·跨语言地道) vs I 前缀(C# 习惯·他处不地道)
whenOtherWins: 如果代码库在 C#/.NET 生态里,IValidationRule 这种 I 前缀反而是官方与团队既定惯例,跟着写才地道;新写 Java/Go/Python 则不用。

termDefinitions.meaning: 在标识符前加类型/用途前缀的老习惯(如接口 IFoo、成员 m_x、字符串 strName)。现代多数语言(Java/Python/Go/Swift)不推荐,认为它冗余且易过时;C# 生态仍保留接口 I 前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hungarian notation prefixes identifiers with their type/role (e.g. interface IFoo, member m_x, string strName). Most modern languages (Java/Python/Go/Swift) discourage it as redundant and stale-prone; the C# ecosystem still keeps the interface I prefix.

scenario: 给变量和方法起名时要不要缩写。
scenario_en: Whether to abbreviate when naming variables and methods.
q: 关于缩写和表意，哪种做法更专业？
q_en: On abbreviations and intent, which is more professional?
options: 尽量缩短，能省字母就省：usr、cnt、calc
用 data、info、manager、handler 这类万能空词就够
变量都叫 a、b、c，反正自己看得懂
options_en: Intent-revealing, no cryptic abbreviations: elapsedMs, userCount
Shorten aggressively, drop letters where you can: usr, cnt, calc
Generic empty words like data, info, manager, handler are enough
Name variables a, b, c — you understand them yourself
optionExplanations: 对：表意命名让读者无需猜;循环里的 i 等公认短名可以,但业务变量要说人话。
错：省字母省不了多少,却大幅增加理解成本。
错：这类词放到任何类上都成立,等于没描述职责。
错：a/b/c 只有你当下懂,面试官和未来的你都要重新猜。
optionExplanations_en: Right: intent-revealing names spare the reader guessing; well-known short names like loop i are fine, but business variables should read plainly.
Wrong: dropping letters saves little but greatly raises comprehension cost.
Wrong: such words fit any class, so they describe no responsibility at all.
Wrong: a/b/c only you understand right now; the interviewer and future-you must re-guess.
why: 名字要表达意图,别含糊缩写:elapsedMs 胜过 e、userCount 胜过 cnt。例外是公认惯例(循环 i/j、坐标 x/y)。也避开 data/info/manager 这类万能空词。清晰 > 简短。
why_en: Names should reveal intent, not use cryptic abbreviations: elapsedMs beats e, userCount beats cnt, retryAttempt beats r. Exceptions are well-known idioms (loop i/j, coordinates x/y). Also avoid catch-all empty words like data/info/manager. Clear > short — an interviewer understanding it at first glance is what reads as professional.
tradeoff: 表意全名 elapsedMs(读者不用猜) vs 短缩写 e/cnt(少敲几个字母·换来理解成本)——清晰 > 简短

scenario: 设计取某个用户的 REST 端点。
scenario_en: Designing the REST endpoint to fetch a user.
q_en: How should you write the resource path?
options_en: Plural nouns, no verbs: GET /users/123, GET /users/123/orders
Verbs in the path: GET /getUser?id=123
Singular nouns: GET /user/123, POST /user
One path per operation: /createUser, /deleteUser, /updateUser
optionExplanations: 对：资源用复数名词,同一 /users 既表集合也表其下的 /users/123,动作交给 HTTP 方法。
错：路径带动词是 RPC 风格,不是 REST;/getUser 里 GET 已表意。
错：单复数混用不一致;主流约定是集合用复数。
错：为每个动作建路径正是 REST 要避免的,动作应由方法承载。
optionExplanations_en: Right: resources are plural nouns; the same /users covers the collection and /users/123 under it, with actions handled by HTTP methods.
Wrong: verbs in the path are RPC-style, not REST; GET already conveys the action in /getUser.
Wrong: mixing singular/plural is inconsistent; the mainstream convention is plural for collections.
Wrong: a path per action is exactly what REST avoids; actions belong to methods.
why: REST 资源路径用复数名词、不带动词:GET /users/123、POST /users、GET /users/123/orders。同一个 /users 既是集合又派生单个资源,一致可预测。动词交给 HTTP 方法,不写进 URL。
why_en: REST resource paths use plural nouns and no verbs: GET /users/123, POST /users, GET /users/123/orders. The same /users is both the collection and the base for a single resource — consistent and predictable. Verbs (create/delete) go to HTTP methods, not the URL.
tradeoff: 复数名词资源路径(动作交给 HTTP 方法) vs 动词路径 /getUser(RPC 风格·端点数随操作膨胀)

scenario: 路径里出现多词资源，比如「用户档案」。
scenario_en: A multi-word resource in the path, e.g. "user profiles".
q: URL 路径段的大小写该怎么写？
q_en: What casing do URL path segments use?
options: snake_case：/user_profiles（下划线，更像数据库风格）
options_en: All-lowercase + kebab-case: /user-profiles
camelCase: /userProfiles
snake_case: /user_profiles (underscores, more of a database style)
PascalCase: /UserProfiles
optionExplanations: 对：URL 惯例是全小写 + 连字符,清晰且避开大小写敏感带来的坑。
错：camelCase 在 URL 里别扭,还可能因大小写敏感出问题。
错：下划线更像数据库/JSON 约定,URL 里少见,还容易被下划线装饰遮住。
错：URL 里用 PascalCase 极不常见。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the URL convention is all-lowercase + hyphens — clear and avoids case-sensitivity pitfalls.
Wrong: camelCase looks awkward in URLs and can break on case sensitivity.
Wrong: underscores are more of a database/JSON convention, rare in URLs, and can hide under link underlines.
Wrong: PascalCase in URLs is highly unusual.
why: URL 路径段用全小写 + kebab-case(连字符):/user-profiles。web 标准约定,比 camelCase(大小写敏感)、snake_case(更像 DB/JSON)都清晰。注意跟 JSON 字段约定不同,别混。
why_en: URL path segments use all-lowercase + kebab-case (hyphens): /user-profiles, /shipping-addresses. This is the web-standard convention — clearer than camelCase (case-sensitivity risk) or snake_case (more DB/JSON). Note this differs from the JSON-field convention; do not mix them.
tradeoff: URL 用 kebab-case(全小写·避开大小写敏感) vs camelCase/snake_case(更像代码标识符或 DB 字段)

termDefinitions.meaning: 全小写、单词间用连字符 - 连接(user-profiles)。因为形似串在扦子上的烤串(kebab)得名。是 URL 路径段的通行约定:清晰、无大小写敏感问题;但不能用于多数编程语言的标识符(- 会被当成减号)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: kebab-case is all-lowercase with words joined by hyphens (user-profiles), named for looking like items on a skewer (kebab). It is the standard for URL path segments — clear and case-insensitive-safe — but cannot be used for identifiers in most languages (the hyphen parses as minus).

scenario: 要「创建一个订单」和「取消一个订单」。
scenario_en: You need to "create an order" and "cancel an order".
options: 全用 GET，动作放在查询参数里：GET /orders?action=create
每个动作用不同端口区分
options_en: Action in the HTTP method: POST /orders, DELETE /orders/9
In the URL: POST /createOrder, POST /cancelOrder
All GET, action in a query param: GET /orders?action=create
Distinguish each action by a different port
optionExplanations: 对：方法本身就是动作词表,客户端与网关看方法即知语义(GET 可缓存、DELETE 幂等)。
错：把动词塞进 URL 是 RPC 风格,丢掉了 HTTP 方法的语义。
错：全 GET 违反语义(GET 应无副作用),还会被缓存/预取误伤。
错：用端口区分动作是奇技淫巧,毫无必要。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the method set is the action vocabulary — clients and gateways read semantics off it (GET cacheable, DELETE idempotent).
Wrong: putting verbs in the URL is RPC-style and discards HTTP-method semantics.
Wrong: all-GET violates semantics (GET must be side-effect-free) and gets hit by caching/prefetch.
Wrong: distinguishing actions by port is a hack with no benefit.
why: REST 里动作由 HTTP 方法承载,不写进 URL:POST 建、GET 读、PATCH 改、DELETE 删。URL 始终只描述资源。所以路径里几乎不该出现 create/get/update/delete 这类动词。
why_en: In REST the action is carried by the HTTP method, not the URL: POST /orders to create, GET /orders/9 to read, PATCH /orders/9 to update, DELETE /orders/9 to delete. The URL always names the resource only. So you should almost never see verbs like create/get/update/delete in a path.
tradeoff: 动作放 HTTP 方法(REST·URL 只指资源) vs 动词写进 URL(RPC 风格·丢方法语义)

scenario: 设计 API 返回的 JSON body 字段名。
scenario_en: Designing the field names in an API JSON body.
q: JSON 字段大小写怎么定最专业？
q_en: How to decide JSON field casing professionally?
options: camelCase 或 snake_case 选一种，全程一致
每个端点随手用不同风格，反正字段名能对上就行
JSON 字段必须和 URL 保持一样，统一都用 kebab-case
options_en: Pick camelCase or snake_case, stay consistent throughout
Use a different style per endpoint at will, as long as field names match up
JSON fields must match URLs and all use kebab-case
JSON fields must use PascalCase
optionExplanations: 对：camelCase(常见于 JS/Node 系)和 snake_case(Stripe/Twitter 等)都可,关键是全程一致。
错：风格不一致会让客户端解析混乱、显得业余。
错：kebab-case 的连字符在多数语言里不能直接做字段名(obj.user-name 报错)。
错：PascalCase 不是 JSON 字段的通行约定(.NET 老风格除外)。
optionExplanations_en: Right: both camelCase (common in JS/Node) and snake_case (Stripe/Twitter) are fine; what matters is consistency throughout.
Wrong: inconsistent styles confuse client parsing and read as amateur.
Wrong: kebab-case hyphens cannot be field names directly in most languages (obj.user-name errors).
Wrong: PascalCase is not the common JSON-field convention (legacy .NET aside).
why: JSON 字段 camelCase 或 snake_case 都行,关键是选一种、全 API 一致。别用 kebab-case(连字符不能当字段名)。注意 URL 用 kebab、JSON 用 camel/snake,两层不同别混。
why_en: JSON body fields can be camelCase or snake_case (camelCase is common in JS/Node; snake_case appears in Stripe, Twitter, etc.) — the key is picking one and staying consistent across the whole API. Do not use kebab-case (hyphens cannot be field names in most languages). Note: URLs use kebab-case while JSON fields use camel/snake — two different layers, do not mix.
tradeoff: JSON 字段 camelCase vs snake_case——两者都专业,取舍不在选哪个,而在全 API 是否一致
whenOtherWins: 如果 API 要兼容 .NET 老客户端,PascalCase 字段可能早已是既定契约——这时保持现有契约优先于换成 camelCase。

scenario: 要「取第 2 页、状态为 active、按创建时间倒序」的用户。
scenario_en: Fetch users on page 2, status active, sorted by creation time descending.
q: 过滤 / 排序 / 分页这些参数放哪？
options: 放进请求体，即使是 GET
options_en: Query params: ?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at
Encoded into the path: GET /users/active/page/2/sort/created-desc
In the request body, even for GET
Passed in HTTP headers
optionExplanations: 对：过滤/排序/分页是对同一集合的「修饰」,用查询参数最贴切、可组合、可省略。
错：把这些编进路径会让路径爆炸,且语义上它们不是资源层级。
错：GET 一般不带 body,很多客户端/代理会忽略它。
错：这类业务参数放 header 不合常规,难发现难调试。
optionExplanations_en: Right: filter/sort/pagination modify the same collection, so query params fit best — composable and optional.
Wrong: encoding them into the path explodes the path and misrepresents them as resource hierarchy.
Wrong: GET usually carries no body; many clients/proxies ignore it.
Wrong: putting business params in headers is unconventional, hard to discover and debug.
why: 过滤、排序、分页用查询参数,不进路径:GET /users?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at。它们是对集合的「修饰」,可组合可省略。路径表达资源层级,query 表达对集合的筛选与视图。
why_en: Filtering, sorting, and pagination go in the query string, not the path: GET /users?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at. They modify the same collection resource — composable and optional. The path expresses resource hierarchy (/users/123/orders); the query expresses filtering and views over a collection.
tradeoff: 过滤/排序/分页放 query(可组合可省略) vs 编进路径(路径组合爆炸·把筛选伪装成资源层级)

scenario: 复盘让 OOD/API 代码显得业余的命名失误。
scenario_en: Review naming mistakes that make OOD/API code look amateur.
q: 下面哪些会让你的代码一眼显得业余？（多选）
q_en: Which make your code look amateur at a glance? (multi-select)
options: 在 Java 里给方法用 snake_case、或在 Python 里给方法用 camelCase
同一个 API 里 JSON 字段一会儿 camelCase 一会儿 snake_case
类名用 PascalCase、方法名跟随语言惯例、常量用 SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
options_en: snake_case methods in Java, or camelCase methods in Python
REST paths written as verbs: POST /createUser, GET /getOrder
JSON fields flip-flopping between camelCase and snake_case within one API
PascalCase classes, methods following the language idiom, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants
optionExplanations: 错误:方法大小写用错语言的惯例,是最刺眼的外行信号。
错误:动词进 URL 是 RPC 风格,丢掉 HTTP 方法语义。
错误:同一 API 内 JSON 风格不一致,客户端解析混乱、显得随意。
这是对的:类 PascalCase + 方法随语言 + 常量全大写,正是专业基线。
optionExplanations_en: Mistake: wrong-language method casing is the most glaring amateur signal.
Mistake: verbs in the URL are RPC-style and discard HTTP-method semantics.
Mistake: inconsistent JSON style within one API confuses clients and reads as careless.
This is correct: PascalCase classes + language-idiomatic methods + all-caps constants is the professional baseline.
why: 三个高频失分:①方法大小写用错语言惯例(Java 写 snake_case)②REST 路径带动词(/createUser)③同一 API 内 JSON 字段风格不一致。正解见前面各卡的组合。
why_en: Four common losses: (1) wrong-language method casing (snake_case in Java); (2) verbs in REST paths (/createUser); (3) inconsistent JSON field style within one API; (4) (the fix) PascalCase classes + language-idiomatic methods + SCREAMING_SNAKE constants + kebab-case URLs. Consistent + idiomatic = professional.
tradeoff: 跟随语言惯例与 REST 约定(专业基线) vs 自创混用风格(省下查约定的时间·换来一眼外行的印象)
